title: Duh - finally leaving fin advisor… how, what next?
body:
O.P.
For the last 15+ years I have been paying a financial advisor to ‘manage my affairs’. Before I was with him, I had a fair amount in Australian Super but he eventually moved me out of that and into managed funds plus cash.
Last financial year my total fees and costs were $23.8k made up of: $10.5k – advisor; $2k Macquarie; $10.8k fund fees. Ugh – and that’s only last year!
Thanks to a friend, my accountant and ChatGPT I have now woken up to the price I’ve paid for someone to soothe my fears and overwhelm around money – and ready to step up to DIY.
I’m 62, working part-time for myself (currently income = expenses). I’d be really grateful for any advice on how to transition most effectively to a safe, simple, easy to manage system – maybe an industry fund and eventually TTR? Would love some ideas. Do I need to think about tax implications?
Btw after I told my advisor I would not be renewing our agreement, he sent me an email saying he was restructuring his business and could now offer me a discount as I was one of his oldest customers! I won’t be taking up that offer.
Here is my current financial situation:
Macquarie Super Consolidator II – Elevate
Aust Listed Securities : $188,000 Vanguard Ethically Conscious AU
Managed Funds: $131,000 Aust Ethical Share $103,000 Loftus Peak Global Disruption $294,000 Vanguard Ethically Conscious $138,000 Hyperion Global Growth
Cash: $93,000 Macquarie Wrap Consolidated $620,000 Macquarie Term Deposits (just matured – not sure if they have automatically rolled over)
My advisor told me that I can’t keep the managed funds without him on my Macquarie account as my advisor. So I don’t think I can remove him until I have transitioned out of those funds.
Thanks in advance for any ideas, wisdom :)
